A8 (G4P): the same for a kernel record with usc_common 0 (k_store_one, k_atomic); 0181.. when the record has a common store
no A8 variant in Orchard's compiler

A10 (G9P): buffer form 2312 0180 8000 (store bit 7 of W1, buffer index in W1, element offset in W2) and address-pair form 2310 .. 8800
A8 (G4P): A8-only address-pair form: W0 size << 11 or 0x0510, W1 0x0500 or reg << 1, W2 0x8100 or pair << 1 (0x0100 for a load), W3 0x4020 (0x0020 for a load). The A9/A10 form completes on the A8 but stores nothing

A10 (G9P): the store's buffer form reads the binding directly
A8 (G4P): built into a register pair: the address comes from the common store (the binding DMA puts the buffer VA in common dwords 0/1); the A9's 64-bit add of a uniform pair faults on the A8; with no offset the A8 moves the two words with the common-store move 0198 03dd 0181/0185 4100 0154 0038

for imm 0x1357 the A10 kernel has 0x38 bytes of code before its 0xc000 run (Orchard: 'a one-store kernel is 0x38 bytes'); the A8 kernel above has 0x52 (0x54 for 0xcafe0001). The difference is the two common-store moves that build the address pair (0x18 bytes) plus the store's fourth word (2 bytes): the A8's store has no buffer form

A10 (G9P): branch_to before the stores, epilogue, jump, 0xc000 padding, 0x8000 at a 64-byte boundary
A8 (G4P): the same (the A8 capture: 0x8000 at kernel + 0x80 after 0xc000 padding)

A10 (G9P): separate PDS and USC bases on the A9
A8 (G4P): one execution base, GPU VA 0x3_00000000 (the PDS heap); USC offsets count from it; the kernel may sit anywhere 64-byte aligned in it (Metal: +0x40 empty, +0x1300 store)
